newsitem.title: UK: LME metals reluctant to step out ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: LME metals reluctant to step out ahead of holiday.

text.p: LME metals largely held within existing boundries on Friday morning, marking time in thin activity ahead of a long weekend.

Some of the metals finished the kerb slightly weaker, but showed little impetus to pile up losses ahead of the UK's holiday on Monday. Most markets slipped in early trading, but put on the brakes and reversed before entering any new, deeper territory.
"It's been very thin with Europe off for May Day yesterday and probably a lot of them are taking today off too," a floor trader said.

Three months copper floated down to $2,336 per tonne after stocks rose by 2,175 tonnes, but light speculative buying lifted prices in the last minutes of the official ring. It ended the morning kerb $10 lower at $2,350.
The spreads narrowed slightly, with the cash/May trading at level after a $5 backwardation on Thursday. The cash/threes spread came in about $10 to a $65/$70 backwardation.
Aluminium followed a similar pattern. Prices slipped to $1,516, nearly filling a gap at $1,514-$1,520, then found support and ended the kerb only $2 easier at $1,626.
Stocks fell by 2,200 tonnes to 795,250 tonnes, down about 15 percent so far this year.
"The fundamentals are strong, but the market doesn't want to hear it. The price is riding on technicals for the moment," a floor trader said.
The market may need more time to consolidate after failing to break above $1,650 on Thursday, analysts said.
Other markets showed the same kind of indecision, skating lower but reversing and finishing the morning with modest gains or losses.
Zinc, however, looked shaky since it breached both the 10-day and 30-day moving averages. It probed $1,255 support and only marginally recovered to finish the morning down $10 at $1,259.
Nickel showed a little more resilience, first looking at $7,270 before rebounding to $7,370, up $20.
Tin held to a tight $40 range, with last business $20 firmer at $5,730, while lead was restricted to a $5 band and shed $2 to $624.
Alloy was last indicated little changed at $1,500/5 against $1,505.
